attacker_pocs.name: empty-bytes-attr
attacker_pocs.why: MultiPartInputFile builds the C++ header by constructing a BytesAttribute for a zero-length bytes value (null data pointer, empty type hint) and then Header::insert copies it. The value constructor skips memcpy when size is 0, but the copy constructor still memcpy's sizeof(unsigned int) bytes out of the zero-length Array. AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow. The real fix only copies when the payload size is greater than zero, so the same file does not overflow.

role_a_rationale: The value constructor matches the upstream fix and no longer calls memcpy on a null source when the payload length is zero. The copy constructor, which Header::insert reaches via BytesAttribute::copy while MultiPartInputFile materializes attributes, uses a different length: a completely empty attribute (no bytes and no type hint) is copied as sizeof(unsigned int) bytes from an Array allocated with size 0. That is a new heap-buffer-overflow, not the original size-zero null memcpy. Non-empty payloads and zero-length attributes that carry a type hint take the safe path, so the existing attribute round-trip test passes under ASan. The golden copy constructor guards with size > 0 and does not read past the empty buffer.
